outcome: Schanuel's conjecture is still open in every source read (latest dated 14 Aug 2026 to 25 Sep 2026); since 26 Jan 2024 the only results touching it are a strengthened statement holding for Lebesgue-almost-all tuples (Waldschmidt, arXiv Apr 2025, Hardy-Ramanujan Journal Apr 2026), a 2026 journal paper giving a single conjecture strictly equivalent to Schanuel plus multiplicative Zilber-Pink (Pila), conditional corollaries and analogues, and a Math Overflow answer on a related question reported as 'answered in 2025' that I could not verify; no proof, disproof, counterexample, or AI-credited result on the conjecture itself was found.
problem_asks: The bullet, as given, asks about 'the transcendence degree of exponentials of linearly independent irrationals'. Unpacked: (1) for every positive integer n; (2) for every n-tuple z_1,...,z_n that is linearly independent over Q; (3) the transcendence degree over Q of Q(z_1,...,z_n, e^{z_1},...,e^{z_n}) is at least n. Two points need care. (a) The bullet says 'irrationals'. Read literally, the z_i are real irrationals, a real-number restriction that the complex statement implies. The standard form, which the Wikipedia article opened for this record gives, is complex numbers linearly independent over Q. Both readings are recorded here; the judging pass should decide which the bullet asks. (b) The statement asks only for the lower bound n, not equality and not algebraic independence of all 2n numbers. The 'strong' form (all 2n numbers algebraically independent) is a separate statement studied in the Waldschmidt paper. (c) For the record, the n=1 case as stated (for z nonzero, the field Q(z, e^z) has transcendence degree at least 1) follows from Lindemann (1882) and Weierstrass (1885): if z is algebraic and nonzero, e^z is transcendental; if z is transcendental, the degree is already at least 1. This is my derivation, not a source's statement. A search summary on the Lindemann-Weierstrass history said the n=1 case is open, which conflicts with this; I have not resolved it against a primary source.

events.what_happened: Lindemann (1882) proved that e^a is transcendental for every nonzero algebraic a, which gives the transcendence of pi. Weierstrass (1885) gave the general Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem: if the algebraic numbers a_1,...,a_n are linearly independent over Q, then e^{a_1},...,e^{a_n} are algebraically independent over Q. These are the earliest settled cases of the conjecture, in the case where the inputs are algebraic. Dates and attributions are from the Wikipedia article on Schanuel's conjecture, which I opened. The primary papers were not read.
events.delivers: Schanuel's bound for tuples of algebraic numbers: for Q-linearly independent algebraic z_1,...,z_n, the exponentials e^{z_i} are algebraically independent over Q, so the transcendence degree is n. Restricted to algebraic inputs.
events.remains: Every tuple with a transcendental entry, and the n >= 2 cases where the exponentials are not known to be algebraically independent. For example, z = (1, pi i) would settle whether e and pi are algebraically independent, and that remains open.
events.direction: Agrees with the conjecture in the algebraic-input case. No counterexample arises here.

events.what_happened: Gelfond and Schneider (1934) proved independently that alpha^beta is transcendental for algebraic alpha not equal to 0 or 1 and irrational algebraic beta. The Wikipedia article on the conjecture, which I opened, lists this as a consequence of the conjecture (obtained by a choice of three numbers). It is recorded as a settled theorem that follows from the conjecture, not as a case of it; whether it counts as a case is for the judging pass.
events.delivers: Transcendence of alpha^beta for algebraic alpha (not 0 or 1) and irrational algebraic beta. A single specific consequence of the conjecture, not a statement about general tuples.
events.remains: All tuples not of this specific shape, including the general statement.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, which implies it.

events.what_happened: Baker proved his theorem on linear forms in logarithms: logarithms of algebraic numbers that are linearly independent over Q are linearly independent over the algebraic numbers. The Wikipedia article I opened says Baker proved this special case in 1966 and that the conjecture would strengthen it. A search snippet gave 1968 for a Baker statement; this is not resolved and the year 1966 is taken from the article.
events.delivers: Linear independence over the algebraic numbers of logarithms of algebraic numbers. This is a case where the exponentials are algebraic. It asserts no algebraic independence, which is what the conjecture asks for that case.
events.remains: Algebraic independence of the logarithms, and every tuple whose exponentials are transcendental.
events.direction: Partial agreement in a special case: the conjecture would strengthen it. No counterexample arises.

events.what_happened: Ax (1971) proved a formal power series (differential-field) analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. The Wikipedia article I opened records this. It is an analogue for functions, not the complex-number statement.
events.delivers: A Schanuel-type transcendence bound for the exponential in a formal power series setting. Analogue only.
events.remains: The complex-number conjecture, which is the bullet's statement.
events.direction: Analogue in a different setting; consistent with the conjecture. Not a statement about complex numbers.

events.what_happened: Bays, Kirby and Wilkie posted 'A Schanuel property for exponentially transcendental powers' (arXiv:0810.4457, submitted 24 Oct 2008, one version). The abstract states that they prove 'the analogue of Schanuel's conjecture for raising to the power of an exponentially transcendental real number', with a more general result for several powers in a setting that includes the complex case. Published Bull. LMS 42 (2010) 917-922. I opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A Schanuel-type lower bound for the power map x -> x^lambda when lambda is an exponentially transcendental real number. The result is about powers, not the exponential map, and it is restricted to real lambda.
events.remains: The conjecture for the exponential map on complex tuples, which is the bullet's statement.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as Bull. LMS 42 (2010), no. 5, 917-922 (DOI 10.1112/blms/bdq054), per the arXiv journal reference.

events.direction: Analogue for powers; consistent with the conjecture. Not a statement about the exponential map.

events.what_happened: Kirby posted 'Exponential algebraicity in exponential fields' (arXiv:0810.4285, submitted 23 Oct 2008; v2 10 Nov 2008 with a minor change to the proof of Lemma 6.2). Published Bull. LMS 42 (2010) 879-890. The abstract states a corollary: there are at most countably many essential counterexamples to Schanuel's conjecture. I opened the arXiv abstract page. Theorem 1.4 itself was not read, so I cannot report its hypotheses.
events.revisions: v1 23 Oct 2008; v2 10 Nov 2008 (minor change to proof of Lemma 6.2); Bull. LMS 42 (2010) 879-890.
events.delivers: A structural partial result: the exponential algebraic closure is a pregeometry with a weak Schanuel property, whose corollary is that there are at most countably many essential counterexamples to the conjecture. Restricted to essential counterexamples. It does not show that no counterexample exists, and it does not prove the conjecture for any particular tuple.
events.remains: Whether any counterexample exists, and the conjecture for every tuple.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (journal of record)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: essential counterexamples, if any, are at most countable. Does not exclude them.

events.what_happened: On the FOM mailing list in October 2015, David Marker reported Angus Macintyre's result from the preprint 'Turing meets Schanuel': if the conjecture has a counterexample, it has one among the recursively coded complex numbers. Marker concluded that the conjecture is equivalent to a Pi^0_3 arithmetic sentence. In a follow-up post the next day he credited Lou van den Dries with strengthening this to primitive recursive counterexamples. A 2017 AMS abstract by Marker states the Pi^0_3 result and the computable-counterexample reduction, using ideas of Jonathan Kirby. The FOM archive pages (2015-October/019265 and 019269) returned HTTP 404 when I fetched them, so the content here comes from the search index excerpt, not the posts themselves. The Macintyre preprint was not found. Marker's suggested Pi^0_2 improvement is unconfirmed.
events.delivers: A logical reformulation: any counterexample can be taken computable, and the conjecture is equivalent to a Pi^0_3 sentence (per Marker's FOM post). Restricted to logical complexity; it establishes nothing about the truth of the conjecture.
events.remains: The truth of the conjecture, which is the content of the Pi^0_3 sentence.

checked_by.qualification: Model theorist; named in Marker's post as the person who noticed the strengthening to primitive recursive counterexamples
checked_by.what_they_did: Observed that Macintyre's result strengthens to a primitive recursive counterexample if one exists (as reported in Marker's follow-up FOM post, seen only through the search index)

events.doubts: Only mailing-list sources and talk abstracts, with the Pi^0_2 improvement suggested but not confirmed; the Macintyre preprint was not located.
events.direction: Logical reformulation: consistent with the conjecture, and sharpens what a counterexample would have to look like. Does not decide the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Viale, 'Forcing the truth of a weak form of Schanuel's conjecture', Confluentes Mathematici 8(2) (2016) 59-83. Journal dates: received 11 Mar 2015, revised and accepted 15 Jul 2016, published 19 Mar 2017. The paper shows, by forcing and Shoenfield absoluteness, that there is a countable algebraically and exponentially closed field K in C relative to which Schanuel's conjecture holds, without the minimality that Wilkie and Kirby obtained. I opened the journal page. The date given is the year of the first submission. A Newton Institute preprint (NI15087) exists in a search result; I did not open it, so the first public date is unconfirmed.
events.revisions: Received 11 Mar 2015; revised 15 Jul 2016; accepted 15 Jul 2016; published 19 Mar 2017 (Confluentes Mathematici, vol. 8, 2016).
events.delivers: A weaker, relative form: for some countable algebraically and exponentially closed K within C, Schanuel's conjecture holds relative to K. Existence only, not minimality, and relative to K rather than Q.
events.remains: The conjecture over Q, and the minimal K.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 15 Jul 2016 and published (per the journal page)

events.direction: Weaker relative statement; consistent with the conjecture. Not a statement about Q.

events.what_happened: Papas, 'Ax-Schanuel for GL_n' (arXiv:1905.04364, v1 10 May 2019; v2 14 Oct 2021). The arXiv abstract page states an Ax-Schanuel type result for exponential maps on upper triangular matrices and then on all of GL_n(C), with an Ax-Lindemann corollary on bi-algebraic subsets. Published in the Israel Journal of Mathematics on 30 Jul 2025 as 'Weak Ax-Schanuel for GLn', per a search summary. The Springer page redirected and was not read, so the journal date is unverified.
events.revisions: v1 10 May 2019 (titled 'Ax-Schanuel for GLn'); v2 14 Oct 2021; journal version 'Weak Ax-Schanuel for GLn' (Israel J. Math., 2025, per search summary).
events.delivers: An Ax-Schanuel type transcendence result for the exponential maps of GL_n(C): a functional statement about these maps, not a statement about complex numbers.
events.remains: The numerical conjecture for complex tuples.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 30 Jul 2025 per a search summary; not verified on the Springer page, which redirected

events.direction: Functional analogue; consistent with the conjecture. Not a statement about the numerical conjecture.

events.what_happened: Blazquez-Sanz, Casale, Freitag and Nagloo, 'A differential approach to Ax-Schanuel, I' (arXiv:2102.03384, v1 5 Feb 2021; v5 1 Jun 2026). The v5 comment reads 'Authors' version to appear in Annals of Mathematics'. Journal acceptance is taken from that comment and is not independently confirmed.
events.revisions: v1 5 Feb 2021; v2 7 May 2021; v3 19 Aug 2022; v4 21 Dec 2023; v5 1 Jun 2026 ('Some changes to Section 7. Authors' version to appear in Annals of Mathematics').
events.delivers: A differential-algebraic Ax-Schanuel theorem with derivatives for uniformizers of simple projective structures on curves. A functional analogue for functions, not for complex numbers.
events.remains: The numerical conjecture for complex tuples.

checked_by.what_they_did: Per the arXiv v5 comment, 'authors' version to appear in Annals of Mathematics'. Not independently confirmed.

events.doubts: A search summary reported that the Annals-version abstract is narrower than earlier arXiv wording. Not verified against the Annals text.
events.direction: Functional analogue; consistent with the conjecture. Not a statement about the numerical conjecture.

events.what_happened: Aslanyan, 'The Existential Closedness and Zilber-Pink Conjectures' (arXiv:2403.09304, submitted 14 Mar 2024). A survey with new results and conjectures on modular versions of Zilber's existential-closedness and Zilber-Pink conjectures, with functional analogues. The abstract does not mention Schanuel's conjecture. I opened the abstract page only; the full text, where a uniform Schanuel remark is said to appear, was not read.
events.revisions: Only the submission date was read; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Survey and modular-analogue results in Zilber's programme. Nothing about Schanuel's conjecture in the abstract.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture itself.
events.direction: Not about the conjecture as stated; the modular analogues are a different problem.

events.what_happened: Waldschmidt, 'Schanuel Property for Elliptic and Quasi-Elliptic Functions' (arXiv:2504.14041, math.NT, submitted 18 Apr 2025, one version). Published in the Hardy-Ramanujan Journal vol. 48 (2025), published 27 Apr 2026 per the journal page. Abstract: 'For almost all tuples (x1,...,xn) of complex numbers, a strong version of Schanuel's Conjecture is true'. The strong version: the 2n numbers x_1,...,x_n, e^{x_1},...,e^{x_n} are algebraically independent over Q. The introduction, read in the arXiv HTML, says this holds 'for Lebesgue measure in C^n'. The paper also gives analogous almost-all statements for z, the Weierstrass functions, zeta, sigma and Serre functions. The paper states its main results are unconditional. The arXiv PDF was binary and unreadable; I read the HTML version up to Section 6.1.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (18 Apr 2025). Journal publication 27 Apr 2026 (HRJ 48, 2025).
events.delivers: For Lebesgue-almost every tuple in C^n (for each n), the 2n numbers x_1..x_n, e^{x_1}..e^{x_n} are algebraically independent over Q. That is stronger than the conjecture's bound of n, so for those tuples the conjecture holds. It says nothing about any particular tuple, including (1, pi i), whose case would settle algebraic independence of e and pi.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture for the tuples in the Lebesgue-null exceptional set in each C^n, including every explicit tuple (for example z = (1, pi i)). The full statement is not settled.

checked_by.who: Hardy-Ramanujan Journal (refereed journal; referees not named on the page)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; the referees are qualified but not named
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (published 27 Apr 2026 per the journal page; an accepted date of 16 Dec 2025 comes from a search summary of the PDF header and is not verified)

events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture: a strong form (2n algebraic independence) holds for almost every tuple. It does not address the exceptional null set, and it does not address any particular tuple.

events.what_happened: Bertolin and Waldschmidt, 'Variations on Schanuel's Conjecture for elliptic and quasi-elliptic functions I: the split case' (arXiv:2504.14048, submitted 18 Apr 2025, one version). The abstract proposes a 'split semi-elliptic Conjecture' for the exponential map of a split extension of an elliptic curve by G_m, says it is equivalent to the Grothendieck-Andre generalized period conjecture for a 1-motive, and says it implies three theorems of Schneider. These are conditional statements about their own conjecture. I opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Conjectures in Schanuel style for an elliptic-extension analogue of G_m, together with conditional implications. Nothing unconditional about the conjecture as stated.
events.remains: Everything about Schanuel's conjecture.
events.direction: Analogue and conditional; does not bear on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Bertolin, 'A conjecture in Schanuel style for 1-motives' (arXiv:2509.08700, v1 10 Sep 2025, v2 26 Nov 2025, v3 29 Jun 2026). The abstract introduces a Schanuel-style conjecture for the semi-elliptic case, states it is equivalent to the Grothendieck-Andre periods conjecture (GAP) for a 1-motive, and states that the GAP conjecture is proved unconditionally for 1-motives defined by an elliptic curve with algebraic invariants and complex multiplication, and for 1-motives defined by torsion points. The page presents Schanuel's conjecture as open and says it is equivalent to GAP for a 1-motive without abelian part. I opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 10 Sep 2025; v2 26 Nov 2025; v3 29 Jun 2026 (refinements; the author says main results and proofs are unaffected).
events.delivers: Unconditional: GAP for certain 1-motives (CM elliptic abelian part with algebraic invariants, and torsion-point 1-motives). Conditional: the semi-elliptic conjecture and a sigma-conjecture. The claimed equivalence of Schanuel's conjecture with a GAP case is a reformulation, not a proof, and no unconditional case of Schanuel's conjecture is delivered.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture; GAP in general.
events.direction: Reformulation plus special cases of a related periods conjecture; does not settle the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Pila, 'Combining the conjectures of Schanuel and Zilber-Pink', Rendiconti Lincei Matematica e Applicazioni 36(3) (2025) 653-670, DOI 10.4171/RLM/1086. Journal dates: submitted 27 Apr 2025, accepted 1 Jul 2025, published 4 Mar 2026. Abstract, verbatim: 'We formulate a conjecture that is strictly equivalent to the conjunction of Schanuel's conjecture and the multiplicative Zilber-Pink conjecture.' No preprint was found, so the date given is the journal publication date, which is the earliest public appearance I could find. The rule is to date the first public written argument, so this date is probably late: a preprint may exist and was not found. The full text is not available to me, and the single conjecture is not named in the abstract.
events.revisions: None found. Journal dates as above.
events.delivers: A single conjecture strictly equivalent to Schanuel's conjecture together with the multiplicative Zilber-Pink conjecture. It establishes no case of Schanuel's conjecture on its own; it is proved only if both are.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture and the multiplicative Zilber-Pink conjecture, both.

checked_by.who: Rendiconti Lincei Matematica e Applicazioni (refereed journal, EMS Press)

events.direction: Reformulation: an equivalence between the conjecture, combined with a second conjecture, and one new statement. It neither proves nor refutes Schanuel's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Berarducci and Gallinaro, 'On the elementary theory of the real exponential field' (arXiv:2603.08365, math.LO, 34 pp., v1 9 Mar 2026, v2 23 Jun 2026, v3 25 Sep 2026). Assuming Schanuel's conjecture, the complete theory of the real exponential field is axiomatized by definably complete exponential fields with exp' = exp, which recovers Macintyre and Wilkie's decidability under the same hypothesis. The model completeness of the axioms for exp restricted to (-1,1) is proved unconditionally. A search summary reports a talk at the Seminaire General de Logique in Paris on 16 Feb 2026, before the arXiv posting; I did not verify this, and under the dating rule the arXiv date is used.
events.revisions: v1 9 Mar 2026; v2 23 Jun 2026; v3 25 Sep 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Conditional on Schanuel's conjecture: an axiomatization of the real exponential field and decidability. Unconditional: model completeness for exp restricted to (-1,1). Does not settle Schanuel's conjecture.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture itself, which is a hypothesis of the main theorem.
events.direction: Conditional consequence; the paper treats Schanuel's conjecture as an unproven hypothesis, which is consistent with it still being open.

events.what_happened: Karatarakis and Wiedijk, 'A formalization of the Gelfond-Schneider theorem' (arXiv:2603.24823, cs.LO, submitted 25 Mar 2026, v1 only). A Lean 4 formalization of the 1934 Gelfond-Schneider theorem. The abstract I read does not mention Schanuel's conjecture and claims no new result. A search excerpt said the work contributes to 'the library of facts supporting the conditional verification of Schanuel's Conjecture'; that sentence does not appear in the abstract page I fetched, so I cannot confirm it.
events.delivers: A machine-checked proof of the Gelfond-Schneider theorem, a settled consequence of the conjecture. No Schanuel result.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture.
events.direction: Formalization of a settled theorem; no direction on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: The UQ benchmark (arXiv:2508.17580, 'UQ: Assessing Language Models on Unsolved Questions', metadata date 26 Aug 2025) uses as Sample #3 a Math Overflow question, cross-posted, about nested sets A_0 = Q and A_{n+1} = S(A_n), where S(F) is the set of positive reals satisfying generalized polynomials with exponents and coefficients in F. Its open questions: whether the chain strictly increases, whether each A_n is a field, and whether e lies in the union. The benchmark's appendix, as far as it was readable, is not decoded here. A search excerpt of the paper reports a poster's reply saying: 'Among my victories against outstanding questions is this one on Schanuel's Conjecture. Asked in 2006 and answered in 2025.' Another search summary says the reply states that Schanuel's conjecture settles some of the questions but not all, and that the paper marks a candidate answer 'Correct (Borderline)'. These are unverified: the paper's text did not decode, the thread was not found, and the UQ question page does not show the Schanuel reply. Separately, the UQ question page lists candidate answers generated by language models and their validation status; see the summary for the names. Only one, o3 Pro, is marked 'UQ Validated; Human Verified', and it is a preview with no visible conclusion. The Schanuel-related reply is conditional on the conjecture for part of the chain question, so it does not settle the conjecture.
events.revisions: arXiv 2508.17580 v1 (metadata 26 Aug 2025). The date of the Math Overflow answer is not known beyond 'answered in 2025' in the excerpt.
events.delivers: As reported in the excerpt and unverified: a conditional answer to part of the A_n chain question, using Schanuel's conjecture. No unconditional result, and nothing about the conjecture itself.
events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture; the parts of the A_n question not settled by the conditional answer (per the excerpt, not all of it). Whether each A_n is a field for n >= 2 is recorded as not known.

checked_by.what_they_did: Gave candidate answers validation statuses; the 'Correct (Borderline)' verdict for the Schanuel-related reply comes from an unverified search summary of the paper

events.doubts: The Schanuel-related reply is known only through an excerpt and a search summary; the thread was not found; the question concerns a related chain of sets, not the conjecture; the candidate answers that were checked failed validation or are pending, except one preview-only o3 Pro answer.
events.direction: A conditional partial answer to a related question. It says nothing about whether the conjecture holds.
people: Unnamed Math Overflow poster who wrote the reply (name not recovered)

events.what_happened: ProofAtlas, 'Schanuel's Conjecture' collaboration page: a read-only beta research workspace that calls itself 'AI-first mathematical research'. It shows the status 'Open conjecture', says 'Revision v6 explicitly reports no proof', and lists background (Ax 1971; the Waldschmidt 2023 survey and 2025 preprint), conditional reductions, and a fixed test case e^{pi^2}, noting that a proof of that case would not by itself prove the full conjecture. It reports about 2,600 retained lines of investigation, most classed as argument development, and says who produced them is not shown. No human contributors and no AI system or model are named; the page refers generically to 'AI agent', 'hosted agent' and 'model runs'. The status check is dated 14 Aug 2026; the page does not give a creation date. I read it through the fetch tool.

events.remains: Schanuel's conjecture in full.
events.time_since_posted: status check 14 Aug 2026 (about 2 months); creation date unknown
events.direction: No direction: no proof is claimed.

summary: Schanuel's conjecture was still open in every source I read, the latest of which are dated Aug to Sep 2026. The Wikipedia article (opened; footer last edited 15 Sep 2026) calls a proof 'a long way off' and cites nothing after 2021. The ProofAtlas status check of 14 Aug 2026 lists it as open with no proof. The Berarducci-Gallinaro v3 of 25 Sep 2026 still assumes it. I found no proof, disproof, or counterexample, and no result on the conjecture credited to any AI system. The in-window items are: (i) Waldschmidt's arXiv paper (18 Apr 2025; Hardy-Ramanujan Journal, published 27 Apr 2026). This is an unconditional strong form, with 2n algebraic independence, that holds for Lebesgue-almost all tuples. It is the strongest in-window result I found, and whether it counts as a restricted case or a different question depends on the measure restriction, which I recorded in the event. (ii) Pila's Rendiconti Lincei paper (published 4 Mar 2026), which formulates one conjecture strictly equivalent to Schanuel plus multiplicative Zilber-Pink; it settles neither. (iii) Conditional and analogue papers: Berarducci-Gallinaro (Mar 2026), Bertolin-Waldschmidt (Apr 2025), Bertolin (Sep 2025, with unconditional cases of a related periods conjecture for 1-motives), Aslanyan's 2024 survey, and the Papas and Blazquez-Sanz Ax-Schanuel analogues (the latter's journal acceptance is by arXiv comment only). (iv) A Math Overflow reply on a related A_n chain question, reported as 'answered in 2025' in an excerpt from the UQ benchmark paper (arXiv 2508.17580). By that excerpt it settles only part of the chain question, conditionally on Schanuel's conjecture. I could not open the thread or decode the paper's appendix, so this rests on unverified text. (v) ProofAtlas, an 'AI-first' workspace, which claims no result and names no system. Pre-window events are recorded for completeness: Lindemann 1882 and Weierstrass 1885 (algebraic inputs; I derived the full n=1 case from them, which conflicts with a search summary that called the n=1 case open), Gelfond-Schneider 1934 and Baker 1966 (consequence and special case), Ax 1971 (analogue), Bays-Kirby-Wilkie and Kirby (Oct 2008, with the countably-many-essential-counterexamples corollary), Marker and Macintyre (Oct 2015, a Pi^0_3 reformulation, with van den Dries' strengthening), Viale (2016, weaker relative form), and two withdrawn claims: Bleybel (2013, claiming Schanuel for C via Zilber's field, withdrawn for errors in section 5) and Marques (2008, withdrawn, a related zeta conjecture). On AI: no system is credited with anything bearing on the conjecture. The only named systems in the records are the language models that generated candidate answers to the A_n chain question on the UQ site (K2-Think, GPT-5, o3 Pro, o4 mini, DeepSeek R1, o3, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4). None of them is validated except one o3 Pro preview with no visible conclusion. I did not list them in ai.systems, because they are not load-bearing for the conjecture. The AI search also covered Erdos-problem results, AlphaProof and AlphaEvolve, OpenAI's May 2026 unit-distance result (not transcendence), Harmonic, Axiom and DeepMind, FrontierMath Open Problems, and ProofAtlas. No Schanuel link appeared in any of them. Caveats: most AI negatives for pre-2026 papers rest on abstracts and metadata, not full texts. competing_reading: Count the Waldschmidt result as a substantial partial result. The quantity the bullet names, the transcendence degree of Q(z, e^z), is what is being bounded, and it is bounded for almost every tuple in a strong form. On this reading the measure restriction is a limit of method rather than a different question. The opposite reading treats the measure-zero exceptional set as the whole difficulty, so nothing about the conjecture as stated has moved. Pila's equivalence could be read as movement, since it ties Schanuel to a Zilber-Pink conjecture that may be easier to attack. Equally it is only a reformulation. The Math Overflow reply could be read as a resolution of a Schanuel-dependent question, but that reading rests on unverified text, and the question is about a different chain of sets.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The full Waldschmidt text, Theorem 22 and Corollary 23 in the HRJ version: the exact measure, whether the strong form is claimed for every n, and whether any sentence claims more than almost all tuples. (b) The full Pila paper, and any preprint dated before April 2026, which would move the event's date. (c) The Math Overflow thread for the A_n chain question, its 2025 reply, the author, the accepted status, and whether AI tools were used. (d) Later papers, 2025 to 2026, that still call Schanuel open without citing Waldschmidt, or any expert note on the almost-all result. (e) The source the bullet's wording came from, to decide whether 'irrationals' means real numbers or complex numbers.

judgement.why: The only in-window event with mathematical content on the conjecture itself is Waldschmidt 2025. I scored it variant, not case. A full-measure set of tuples is not a restriction the statement names. More importantly, the conjecture's own bound (transcendence degree at least n) holds for almost every tuple trivially, because tuples whose entries are algebraically dependent form a countable union of proper algebraic subvarieties, which has measure zero. So for the question as stated, the paper's new content is the strong 2n form. That is a different, stronger statement, and every explicit tuple is left untouched. Pila is an equivalence with a conjunction, Berarducci-Gallinaro is conditional, the Bertolin papers concern analogues and periods, ProofAtlas claims nothing, and the UQ item is about a different question; I scored all of these none. Before the snapshot, Lindemann-Weierstrass settles the case of algebraic inputs, so it is a case. Gelfond-Schneider and Baker are consequences or weaker forms rather than restrictions of the transcendence-degree claim, so I scored them variant. Bleybel's whole-problem claim was withdrawn. No AI system produced any mathematics: ProofAtlas and UQ name no system in ai.systems.
judgement.doubts: The triviality argument for the n-bound on almost all tuples is my own reasoning, not a source's; it supports variant over case for Waldschmidt. Calling Gelfond-Schneider and Baker variant rather than case is a judgement call, but it only affects pre-snapshot rows. The 'irrationals' wording (real versus complex) does not change any answer.
